title: Can one finger move a 100,000-tonne ship?
caption:
One finger can move a 100,000-tonne ship. 🚢☝️

On land, static friction holds a heavy object still until you push hard enough. Water has no static friction: a hull at rest in still water moves in response to the slightest force. Push a ship the size of an aircraft carrier (about 100,000 t) with 10 newtons, roughly the weight of a 1 kg bag, and it accelerates at 0.0000001 m/s². After one minute it has moved about 0.2 mm; after an hour of steady pushing, about 65 cm, drifting at roughly 1.3 m per hour.

The catch is momentum: to stop it again you'd have to push back just as hard for another hour. In a real harbour, wind, current and mooring lines easily overpower a finger, which is why ships need tugs.
